title: Redis cache outage
description: Walk a derived-cache loss. Primary remains authoritative. Stampede and stale-if-error are product choices, not magic.
assumptions: Redis is derived. PostgreSQL (or the selected primary) owns rows.
Cache-aside: miss hits the primary. Write-through is not this walkthrough.
TokenX settlement is not served from Redis.

steps.title: Healthy cache-aside
steps.timeline: t0: app reads Redis then primary on miss. TTL or explicit versioning.
steps.inFlight: GET cache; on miss GET primary then SET cache.
steps.consistency: Hits can be stale up to TTL. Primary is source of truth.
steps.durability: Cache is rebuildable. Primary WAL/commit is unchanged.
steps.userVisible: p99 includes cache RTT on hit; miss includes primary.
steps.recovery: Not in this step. Watch hit rate and primary QPS.

steps.title: Detect cache unavailability
steps.timeline: t1: Redis process, shard, or network dies. Timeouts exceed the cache budget (example: 50–200 ms).
steps.inFlight: In-flight GETs to Redis fail. App must fail open to primary or fail closed per API.
steps.consistency: No cache does not mean the primary is wrong.
steps.durability: No cache durability loss of authoritative rows.
steps.userVisible: Latency spike if every request hits primary. Errors if the app treats cache as required.
steps.recovery: Do not failover the primary because Redis died.

steps.title: In-flight cache operations
steps.timeline: t1–t2: SET/GET in flight have no cache outcome.
steps.inFlight: Lost SETs are fine. Lost GETs must fall through. Write-behind queues if any are a separate RPO.
steps.consistency: Clients may see mix of stale hits (before death) and fresh primary reads.
steps.durability: Write-behind not yet on primary is a loss window you must have named earlier — illegal for TokenX.
steps.userVisible: Timeouts then slower 200s, or 5xx if fail-closed on cache.
steps.recovery: Drop write-behind if you cannot prove primary apply.

steps.title: No cache promotion
steps.timeline: t2: there is no replica of Redis that becomes authoritative.
steps.inFlight: Do not promote a replica cache as a ledger.
steps.consistency: Primary remains the only write authority.
steps.userVisible: Degraded mode banner optional; correctness banner required if you shed.
steps.recovery: Keep serving from primary with admission control.

steps.title: Client and app retries
steps.timeline: t2–t3: clients retry GETs. Write retries still need idempotency keys.
steps.inFlight: Retry amplification onto the primary is the real failure.
steps.consistency: Retries of reads are safe. Retries of writes are not unless keyed.
steps.userVisible: 429 if you shed. UNKNOWN on write timeouts.
steps.recovery: Bound retries, jitter, and a primary concurrency limiter.

steps.title: Consistency during stampede
steps.timeline: t3: thundering herd on popular keys.
steps.inFlight: Many concurrent primary reads for one key.
steps.consistency: Single-flight / request coalescing is optional but recommended. Still not linearizable across clients.
steps.recovery: Coalesce, serve stale-if-error only if the product allows stale.

steps.title: Restore Redis
steps.timeline: t4: Redis returns empty or with leftover TTL data.
steps.inFlight: Warm from primary on miss. Do not bulk-load stale snapshots as truth.
steps.consistency: Cold cache is cache misses, not wrong commits.
steps.userVisible: Latency returns as hit rate recovers.

steps.title: User-visible outcome
steps.timeline: End state: primary survived; some users saw slowness or shed reads.
steps.inFlight: None required to be replayed for cache GETs.
steps.consistency: If you served stale-if-error, say so. TokenX never did.
steps.userVisible: Degraded catalog OK; money APIs fail closed without cache only if you wrongly required it.
steps.recovery: Incident review: why cache was on the critical path.
